# 72-Hour Power Outage: Home Field Guide

Prepare an ordinary household to ride out a temperate-climate outage up to 72 hours safely and comfortably, no generator. Do sections in order; earliest matter most.

## Water
Store 4 L per person daily — 12 L each for 72 hours: half drinking, half cooking and hygiene. Use food-grade containers, out of direct sunlight, replaced every 6 months. If a storm is forecast, also fill the bathtub — for flushing toilets and washing, never drinking.

## Food
Keep a 3-day shelf of no-cook non-perishables: canned beans, canned fish, peanut butter, crackers, dried fruit, shelf-stable milk. Own a manual can opener; electric is useless. Eat refrigerator food first, then freezer, then this shelf.

## Fridge and freezer
Unopened fridge stays safe ~4 hours. Full freezer holds ~48 hours, half-full only ~24, so keep it consolidated and full, even with frozen-water containers. Keep both doors shut; tape a reminder note to each. Discard any perishable over 2 hours above 4°C — when in doubt, throw it out.

## Light
Use battery LED lanterns or headlamps; avoid candles, a leading cause of outage house fires. Keep at least one light per person plus two spare battery sets each. A headlamp by every bed, a lantern in the kitchen, findable in the dark.

## Heat and safety
Never run a camping stove, barbecue, or generator indoors, in a garage, or near a window — all make carbon monoxide, odourless and fatal. Install at least one battery CO alarm per sleeping floor. In cold, pick one small south-facing room, shut the door, gather everyone; layered clothing and blankets beat any improvised heater. Below 10°C indoors with no way to stay warm, move to a warming centre or neighbour's.

## Communication
Keep a battery or hand-crank radio for broadcasts; learn your local emergency station frequency beforehand. Charge every phone and power bank when a storm is forecast — a full 20,000 mAh bank recharges a typical phone about 4 times. Set low-power mode at the start; pre-agree one out-of-area contact everyone texts, since texts beat voice on congested networks.

## Medical
Keep a first-aid kit and a 7-day supply of every prescription, rotated to stay in date. Refrigerated medicine like insulin usually lasts 28 days at room temperature, but confirm your specific drug with a pharmacist beforehand. Write pharmacy, doctor, and poison-control numbers on paper — a dead phone is no phone book.

## When power returns
Wait 5 minutes before switching major appliances on, letting the grid stabilise. Check the freezer: food still holding ice crystals can refreeze safely. Restock everything used within a week, water and batteries first. Write a one-page note on what was missing or awkward, and fix at least one gap before the next outage.
